paper.title: Online Bidding for Contextual First-Price Auctions with Budgets under One-Sided Information Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Contextual first-price auctions with budgets under one-sided information feedback (scalar context)
unmapped: Repeated first-price auction: bid b_t in [0,v_t], reward (v_t-b_t)1{b_t>d_t}, pay b_t on win
One-sided (censored) feedback: highest competing bid observed only after a loss
Competing bid D_t = alpha X_t + Z_t with unknown coefficient alpha and unknown noise CDF G
Private value v_t = f(x_t) observed before bidding
Learner knows rho, domain bounds x_bar, v_bar, z_bar, alpha_bar and numerical bounds g_max, g_min, kappa
settings.definition_quote: Consider a bidder participating in repeated first-price auctions over a horizon $T$ with total budget $B=\rho T$... We consider one-sided information feedback. After a losing round $b_t\le d_t$, the highest competing bid $d_t$ is observed. After a winning round $b_t>d_t$, the bidder observes the winning outcome and her own payment, but not $d_t$. The competing bid follows the contextual model $D_t=\alpha X_t+Z_t$

settings.name_in_paper: Structured multi-dimensional extension (contexts on a monotone one-dimensional manifold)
unmapped: Repeated first-price auction with hard budget and one-sided censored feedback
Competing bid D_t = <alpha, X_t> + Z_t with alpha in known compact convex Theta subset R_+^d, unknown G
Contexts X_t = h(S_t) on a monotone one-dimensional manifold, f(h(s)) strictly increasing
Learner knows Theta, rho, domain bounds and g_max, g_min, kappa
settings.definition_quote: Let the highest competing bid satisfy $D_t=\langle\boldsymbol\alpha,\mathbf X_t\rangle+Z_t$, with $\boldsymbol\alpha\in\Theta\subset\mathbb R_+^d$... We consider contexts on a monotone one-dimensional manifold $\mathbf X_t=h(S_t)$, $S_t\in[0,1]$

algorithms.name: Bidding Algorithm for Contextual First-Price Auctions with Budgets (quantile-based estimator + bid elimination + dual update)

symbols.v_bar: known upper bound on private values
symbols.C_stat: statistical factor v_bar(1+v_bar g_max+kappa_V^{-1/2})+(1+v_bar g_max) x_bar (C_init + C_alpha)
symbols.T_star: horizon threshold given by explicit sufficient conditions (eq. explicit-large-horizon)

conditions: Assumption 1: noise density bounded by g_max, Lipschitz and >= g_min near the 0.99-quantile
Assumption 2: bounded contexts, values, noise, alpha; i.i.d. mutually independent contexts and noise
Assumption 3: local quantile identifiability with constants kappa, r_id; X atomless
Assumption 4: visibility of high competing bids with margin Delta_q
Assumption 6: value density bounded above and below on [0, v_bar]

source.label: thm:main-regret
source.quote: Under Assumptions~\ref{ass:lipschitz}, \ref{ass:bounded}, \ref{ass:identifiability}, \ref{ass:visible-quantile}, \ref{ass:effective-value-margin}, and~\ref{ass:value-density}, Algorithm~\ref{alg:budget-bidding}, with the step size in~\eqref{eq:budget-scaled-stepsize}, satisfies $\operatorname{Regret}(\pi) \le C(1+\frac{\bar v}{\rho}) \mathcal C_{\mathrm{stat}}\sqrt T\log T$ for every $T\ge T_\star$, where $C$ is a universal numerical constant.

results.notes: Regret defined as R(pi*) - R(pi), expected reward against optimal hard-budget policy; recorded as pseudo_regret since defined via expectations of policy rewards. Universal constant C omitted via O notation. Paper summarizes as O~(sqrt T). Mapping of one-sided feedback to partial_monitoring and the auction to continuum_other is approximate.

symbols.C_alpha: 4 C_q / kappa with C_q = 2 c_vc / g_min, c_vc = 1024
symbols.n_A: number of estimation samples |A_i| in phase i

conditions: initial-localization event holds with beta_0 <= r_id
b_j <= v_j for all j in A_i

source.label: thm:main-estimation
source.quote: Conditional on an initial exploration history for which the initial-localization event holds, if $\beta_0\le r_{\mathrm{id}}$, then with probability at least $1-\delta$, $|\hat\alpha_i-\alpha|\le C_\alpha\sqrt{\log(2|A_i|/\delta)/|A_i|}$, where $C_\alpha:=4C_q/\kappa$.

results.notes: Estimation error of the contextual coefficient by the quantile-based estimator (Algorithm quantile), not a regret bound.

symbols.v_bar: known upper bound on private values
symbols.C_stat_d: v_bar(1+v_bar g_max+kappa_V^{-1/2})+(1+v_bar g_max) x_bar (4 z_bar sqrt(d/kappa_h) + 4 C_q L sqrt(d)/kappa); order d^{3/2} when L=O(d)

conditions: Assumptions 1, 6, structured vector contexts (monotone 1-D manifold, Cov(h(S)) >= kappa_h I), multi-dimensional effective-value margin, visibility, identifiability

source.label: prop:multi-dimensional-guarantee
source.quote: Fix a finite dimension $d$ and $L\ge d+1$. With the step size in~\eqref{eq:budget-scaled-stepsize}, Algorithm~\ref{alg:multi-budget-bidding} satisfies $\operatorname{Regret}(\pi) \le C(1+\frac{\bar v}{\rho}) \mathcal C_{\mathrm{stat},d}\sqrt T\log T$ for every $T\ge T_\star(d)$... giving $\widetilde O(d^{3/2}\sqrt T)$ regret.

results.notes: With L=O(d) and other parameters fixed, paper states O~(d^{3/2} sqrt T). Compute not clearly polynomial since estimator minimizes over a d-dimensional set.
